children: GE Vernova, the power-equipment and grid-technology company

, slipped approximately 1% to $953 at 11.04am in the September 30 session as AI developers face a costly choice: wait for grid connections or pay for on-site power. Smaller turbines offer a faster route to getting servers running. That puts GE Vernova in a strong commercial position, but speed comes with a bill.

Crusoe's orders cover 29 LM2500XPRESS turbine packages capable of supplying nearly one gigawatt combined, including ten units for its Abilene campus. The opportunity extends beyond turbines: GE Vernova reported more than $5 billion in first-half data-center orders within its Electrification segment, already exceeding twice its full-year 2025 total. The GF Score graphic shows just 21 out of 100, a reminder that booming orders alone do not establish a strong overall investment case.

The customer economics deserve scrutiny. According to Reuters, an Electric Power Research Institute specialist estimates that smaller turbines can carry capital costs per unit of electricity up to 50% above larger alternatives. Developers may accept that premium to bring computing capacity online sooner. For investors, the question is how much of today's urgency becomes repeat business once grid connections and larger power plants catch up.

title: GE Vernova Stocks Slip as Data Centers Choose Faster Turbines
